questions.question: What is an independent clause?
options: A clause that can stand alone as a complete sentence
A clause that always begins with "because"
A clause without a verb
A question
questions.explanation: Independent clauses are complete sentences on their own; dependent clauses need an independent clause.

questions.question: What do the FANBOYS conjunctions do?
options: Join two ideas of equal weight
Introduce dependent clauses
Replace punctuation entirely
Mark the end of a paragraph
questions.explanation: FANBOYS (for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so) are coordinating conjunctions joining equal, independent ideas.

questions.question: Which of these correctly joins two closely related independent clauses without a conjunction?
options: "The exam was difficult; many students struggled."
"The exam was difficult, many students struggled."
"The exam was difficult many students struggled."
"The exam was difficult: because many students struggled."
questions.explanation: A semicolon links two closely related independent clauses. A comma alone creates a comma splice.

questions.question: What are the three types of dependent clauses?
options: Adverbial, relative and noun clauses
Long, short and medium clauses
Past, present and future clauses
Formal, informal and neutral clauses
questions.explanation: Dependent clauses are adverbial (when, because), relative (who, which) or noun clauses (that, what).

questions.question: Why does sentence variety matter in writing?
options: It keeps readers engaged, creates rhythm and lets you emphasise key ideas
Examiners count the number of words only
Identical sentences are easier to read
It makes the text longer automatically
questions.explanation: Varying structure, openings and length creates engaging rhythm and demonstrates advanced language skills.
